handoff: Scope and design are right and every test tier passed. Blocking: no test runs a tick and checks the timing it records (observe phases and call counts, Actor ms, sync/timing in the record, tick.end slowest, heartbeat last_tick_ms in the view). Also minor: renewal batch time counted per claim, no separate process phase; nit: act_ms includes the tick.start write.

findings.title: No test runs a tick and checks the timing it records
findings.criterion: Wanted: observe broken down with the number of calls; each action's time in its result; slowest phase visible; last tick's duration in status
findings.detail:
The new tests (packages/cli/test/unit/tick-timing.test.ts, records.test.ts, view.test.ts, cockpit-tui.test.ts) only cover pure helpers fed hand-built inputs. Nothing checks that observe really times base_fetch/local/sync.*/runner/stories and counts list_issues/get_issue/find_pr/pr_ci (observe/index.ts:125-228), that Actor.run fills ms, batch time included (act/index.ts:52-65), that runTick writes timing+sync into the appended tick record and slowest on tick.end (tick.ts:300-343), or that markTick → lastTickMs → loadProjectView carries last_tick_ms (heartbeat.ts:453-461, load.ts:501). The spec asks: 'Every tick record carries how long each phase took… with the number of calls'. Leaving out any one of the timer.time/timer.count wraps, or the markTick argument, would keep every test green. A dev-build smoke is not a regression test.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add one cli integration test on createHarness (FakeRemote with one story): run a sync tick, read the day's trace, and assert that the tick record validates and has sync.ran, timing.observe keys including base_fetch/sync.issues/sync.stories/local, timing.calls {list_issues:1, find_pr:≥1}, and a numeric result.ms on each decision; that tick.end has slowest; and that loadProjectView(...).heartbeat.last_tick_ms is a number.

findings.title: A batched renewal's time is counted again for each claim, which can make it the slowest phase
findings.detail:
Every renewed decision gets ms = renewMs, the whole batch's time. tickTiming then gives each one its own candidate 'act claim <unit>' carrying the full batch time. With N renewals, slowest names one arbitrary unit with the batch time, and the result.ms values add up to N× the real time. This is documented in the recipe and the schema comment, but slowest names a unit that is not to blame on its own.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Optionally give the batch one candidate ('act claim (N renewals)') in tickTiming, or leave it as is and keep the documentation.

findings.title: The 'process' phase from the Wanted list has no timing of its own
findings.detail:
The spec lists 'local facts, per-story git, runner, process'. Process liveness probes run inside loadLocalFacts (the lease liveness) and inside the per-story loop, so their time is folded into 'local' and 'stories'. That is acceptable for a quick round, but it is not called out in the handoff or the recipe.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Say in the recipe that process probes count under local/stories, or time ports.process calls separately.

findings.title: act_ms includes writing tick.start and building the Actor
findings.detail:
tAct is taken before appendTrace(tick.start) and new Actor(). The handoff mentions this, but the schema comment does not.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Take tAct after new Actor(), or note it in the TickTiming doc comment.
